reading.body:
CyrusOne's Norwalk, Connecticut campus publishes 4 MW of IT capacity, half of the state's 8 MW total and small enough that it is not a frontier AI node.

Connecticut has 5 mapped data center facilities and 8 MW of published IT load. Norwalk holds half of that. The rest is spread across the remaining sites, and most mapped facilities publish no capacity figure at all, so the state total is a floor rather than a full accounting. The facility carries SSAE 16 Type II certification, which speaks to audited security and availability controls and says nothing about compute.

The 168,000 square feet of technical space against 4 MW works out to roughly 24 watts per square foot. That is a low ratio for a building of that size, and it points to power as the limiting input rather than floor area. For AI specifically, the number that governs what a site can run is delivered megawatts, not square footage. At 4 MW, Norwalk can host a modest cluster but not a large training campus.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. No announced expansion is recorded, so the suitability score of 49 is calculated without knowing whether the site will grow. Nothing here describes the grid connection, the generation source, or the price of electricity, which are the inputs that would decide whether the site could scale. Capacity at the other Connecticut facilities is unpublished, so the state figure could be higher. The record also carries no street address or coordinates, so proximity to transmission or fiber cannot be assessed.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
